approachQuestion.prompt:
Union coverage

Given closed integer intervals [start,end] with start≤end, return the number of integer points covered by at least one interval. Intervals can overlap or touch. 1≤n≤200000; endpoints are within ±10^9; answer fits signed 64-bit. Examples: [[1,3],[3,5],[8,8]]→6; [[-2,-2]]→1.

Do not modify either input. Values are opaque comparison keys; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside the stated model. Choose the most efficient valid method that returns the required result for every allowed input.
constraints: Inputs are read-only and must remain unchanged.
Only comparison-based ordering is allowed; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside this problem model.

options.text: Sort intervals by start, merge overlapping or touching intervals, and add each merged length.
options.feedback: Merged ranges are disjoint; inclusive integer length is end−start+1.
Overlaps are double-counted: [[1,3],[3,5]] yields 6 instead of 5.

options.text: Sort by end and merge only when intervals are identical.
options.feedback: Different overlapping ranges still cover shared points.

options.text: For each integer coordinate, test whether any interval covers it and increment a counter when covered.
options.feedback: The numeric domain is enormous and the stated model excludes coordinate enumeration. For [[-1000000000,1000000000]], this visits billions of coordinates instead of processing the intervals by comparisons.

feedback.reason: A sorted range can extend the current union or start a new gap.
details: Sort by start, maintain the current merged end, and accumulate inclusive lengths whenever a gap begins.
A sorted range can extend the current union or start a new gap. Inclusive endpoints require end-start+1 when closing a merged run. Summing original lengths double-counts overlap.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed below, choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Count working copies, event/heap/visited storage and sort buffers; exclude the caller input and returned output. Comparisons and arithmetic take constant time; merge sort uses a linear buffer.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Sort intervals, then accumulate lengths of disjoint merged runs.
details: At each of logarithmically many merge levels, all n copied intervals participate in linear total merging work, giving O(n log n). The subsequent union scan consumes each interval once. The immutable-input copy and reusable merge buffer each hold n intervals, so O(1) space omits live helper storage; quadratic time overcounts repeated comparisons absent from this method.
